lessons.title: Where to Find Transcripts: BSE/NSE Filings, Company IR Pages, and Screener.in

body.text: The transcript is public, free, and one search away. Most retail investors never open it.

children.text: This is not hidden information. Under SEBI's LODR Regulation 30, every listed company must disclose the audio recording of an earnings call or investor meet and post a written transcript, and keep both available for years afterward. The transcript is filed with the stock exchanges exactly the way the results themselves are, which means it is a few clicks away for any company you already track.

children.text: Route 1: Go Straight to BSE or NSE

On bseindia.com, search the company by name or scrip code and open its corporate announcements, then filter for the earnings call transcript or investor presentation category. NSE's corporate filings section under nseindia.com works the same way. This is the official, unedited filing, the same document the company legally submitted, but the interface is built for compliance search, not comfortable reading, and the PDFs are not always neatly text searchable.
Route 2: The Company's Own Investor Relations Page

Most large and mid cap companies, think Titan Company, Asian Paints, or HDFC Bank, maintain a dedicated Investor Relations section that archives transcripts, investor presentations, and often the audio or webcast recording itself, organized quarter by quarter going back several years. It is usually easier to browse a company's history here than through exchange filings. The catch is that this archive is not separately mandated, it is the same filing republished, so its depth and organization vary a lot once you move down the market cap ladder.

Every company page on screener.in has a Concalls entry under Documents, sitting right next to annual reports and credit ratings. It lists the transcript PDF filed with the exchange alongside Screener's own short notes summarizing the call, and usually the investor presentation too. Since you are probably already on the company's screener.in page reading the results, this is the fastest route from the numbers to the primary source.

body.text: Screener's concall notes are a fast index, not a substitute. Compressing an hour long call into a page of bullet points means tone, hedging, and exactly how a question got dodged rarely survive the summary. Use the notes to decide which transcripts are worth reading in full, not as the final read.

body.label: Screener.in
body.description: Search any NSE or BSE listed company, then open the Documents section on its page for the Concalls list: transcript, Screener's notes, and the investor presentation.

body.title: Your First Transcript Hunt
steps: Pick a company you already track on screener.in
Open its screener.in page and find the Concalls entry under Documents
Open the transcript PDF for the most recent quarter, not just Screener's notes
If the transcript is missing on screener.in, search the company name directly on nseindia.com under Corporate Filings, or bseindia.com under Corporate Announcements
Check the company's own Investor Relations page for an audio recording or webcast if you want tone as well as words
Note the date of the concall against the date the transcript appeared, SEBI allows up to 5 working days for the written version

points: SEBI's LODR Regulation 30 requires listed companies to post the concall audio within 24 hours and the written transcript within 5 working days, retained for at least 8 years
BSE and NSE filings are the official, unedited source, but built for compliance search rather than easy reading
Company IR pages republish the same filings, often archived more conveniently by quarter, though depth varies by company
Screener.in's Concalls section is the fastest way to jump from the numbers to the transcript, but its own notes are a summary, not a replacement for reading the full transcript
Checking one of these three sources every time you check a result is what turns reading about a concall into actually reading it
